Measured on 16 public tables (UCI and PMLB), held-out real test rows. Robust retention is the worst of three auditor families (linear/logistic, CatBoost, MLP) trained only on the method's rows; medians over tables with 95% bootstrap intervals.

| Method | Median bytes | Robust retention | Tables ≥ 0.9 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| DOPE, 2 KiB budget | 2.0 KiB | 0.905 [0.815, 0.939] | 8/16 |
| **DOPE, 4 KiB budget** | 3.8 KiB | 0.909 [0.843, 0.932] | 9/16 |
| DOPE, 16 KiB budget | 5.7 KiB | 0.933 [0.869, 0.965] | 10/16 |
| DOPE research kernel (`dope-kernel fit-table`) | 1.1 KiB | 0.677 [0.484, 0.844] | 3/16 |
| Real rows, xz-compressed to 4 KiB | 4.0 KiB | 0.340 [-4.012, 0.918] | 5/16 |

| Gaussian copula (SDV defaults) | 82.0 KiB | 0.282 [0.094, 0.447] | 1/16 |
| ARF (arfpy defaults) | 673.1 KiB | 0.705 [0.000, 0.856] | 3/16 |

Transfer Description Length at τ = 0.9: DOPE reaches it on 11/16 tables (median 1.9 KiB); xz-compressed real rows reach it on 16/16 (median 50.8 KiB).
At equal bytes, wherever DOPE fits the budget, it beats xz-compressed real rows in 60 of 92 paired (table, budget) comparisons and loses 32 (wins/ties/losses by budget: 1 KiB 11/0/1, 2 KiB 14/0/2, 4 KiB 11/0/5, 8 KiB 10/0/6, 16 KiB 10/0/6, 64 KiB 4/0/12). DOPE could not fit within 1 KiB on 4 tables: the schema plus the leanest program alone exceeded that budget.
Against the repository's research kernel (median 1.1 KiB) on the 14 regression and binary tables it supports, DOPE's robust retention wins/ties/losses are at 1 KiB 9/0/5, Hodges–Lehmann +0.010 [-0.394, +0.126]; at 2 KiB 12/0/2, Hodges–Lehmann +0.166 [+0.047, +0.291]; at 4 KiB 11/0/3, Hodges–Lehmann +0.160 [+0.045, +0.306]. On the 2 multiclass tables the kernel refuses the target or fits its class codes as a regression; its row above counts them as measured.

#### 2. `DOPE-MLC-v3`: 1,069-Dataset (4,276-Cell) Four-Tier Multi-Task Study (`Small` 2 KiB, `Medium` 4 KiB, `High` 16 KiB, `Ultra` 64 KiB)

**`DOPE-MLC-v3`** adds `16` global + `7` per-column + `8` heteroscedastic/tail + `20` multiclass simplex mathematical building-block probes (`asinh`, `atan`, `erf`, `cbrt`, `log1p`, invariant row summaries, `tanh`, `expm1`, `clamp`, `step`, `hinge`, `sin/cos`, `fract`, `hypot`, `atan2`, normalized difference ratio), `48` inter-landmark summary statistics + `InterLandmarkAttentionBlock` (`vec256 = 140 + 48 + 68`), an active per-column gate head (`col_gate_head` wired into loss, encoding, and generation; `grad_norm = 0.000721`), a fourth **`Small` (`2,048 B`)** complete-envelope byte tier (`DML3` header + `CSC1` compact scaler sidecar included in cap), and native multiclass synthesis (`LR-VLOT` shared-split vector-leaf oblivious trees).
- **Maximized-Training (`96.74%` Loaded Train, `< 5%` Validation) Disjoint-1,069 Convergence & Matched-Budget `A0..A3` Ablation (`task-4221`, `v3_maxtrain97_val3pct_convergence_receipt.json` `9e218519...`, `v3_maxtrain97_corpus_exposure_and_split_manifest.json` `1c75ff09...`):** Because `load_v3_episode_pool` loads `1` cell (`splits[0]`) per dataset passing `20 <= n_tr <= 1,800` and `p <= 80`, the actual loaded episode pool comprises **`2,229` loaded training cells (`96.7448%`, `1,997` reg/bin + `232` mc) and `75` loaded `dev_val` cells (`3.2552% < 5%`, `40` reg + `17` bin + `18` mc) = `2,304` loaded episode cells** (`76 / 2,311 = 3.2886% < 5%` on the catalog manifest before `n_tr`/`p` filter [`6` train + `1` `dev_val` skipped]; `2.8876%` is a 6-split reference ratio not loaded by `v3`; `1,000` `v2`-panel + `69` multiclass eval datasets strictly excluded with `0` overlap). Across `8` training rounds (`R1: 558` visits + `R2..R8: 557` visits/round = **`4,457` cumulative episode visits**, `batch_accum = 16`, `280` scheduled optimizer updates, **`4,457 / 2,229 = 1.999551×` effective full-population passes** per variant), `100%` (`75/75`) `dev_val` loss for `A3` improves from `0.69727 ± 0.03888 [0.62909, 0.76794]` (`R0`) $\to$ **`0.68492 ± 0.03877 [0.60885, 0.76099]`** (`R8*`, `-1.77%`; `Small 0.69473 / Med 0.69128 / High 0.67958 / Ultra 0.67408`; driver `0.04143`; `600`-cell train monitor `0.47454 -> 0.46132`). Under matched `4,457`-visit budgets (`200×` dataset-grouped bootstrap across `75` datasets), `A0` reaches `0.68700 ± 0.04276` (`R5`; `0.68709` at `R8`), `A1` reaches `0.68531 ± 0.03433` (`R7`; `0.68547` at `R8`), `A2` reaches `0.68489 ± 0.03877` (`R8`), and `A3` reaches `0.68492 ± 0.03877` (`R8`, `dope_mlc_v3_maxtrain97_best.pt` `77ffb94f...`, with `A2` and `A3` within `0.00003` — `< 0.001× SE` — on the 75-dataset `dev_val` set while `A3` provides active `col_gate_head` gradient flow `0.001014`).

  - **`DOPE-MLC-v3` vs. `DOPE-MLC-v2` (`dope_mlc_v2_wire`, `Elo = 1538.0 [1531.8, 1543.2]` on `9,000` Supported Cells):** On the `1,000` regression/binary datasets at `Medium`/`High`/`Ultra` (`9,000` cells; `v2` lacks a `Small` `2 KiB` tier or native `multiclass` head), `v3` and `v2` tie within `0.10` on `8,136 / 9,000` cells (`2,843` within `0.01`), with `v3` trailing `v2` by `mean ΔR = -0.0084 [-0.0104, -0.0063]` (`W/T_010/L = 392 / 8,136 / 472`) because `v3` allocates budget to the `CSC1` raw-domain sidecar and multi-task head inside the wire cap.
  - **`DOPE-MLC-v3` vs. `rows_wire` (`RWW1`, `Elo = 1597.3 [1589.7, 1606.1]`):** Across all `12,828` cells under the bounded `340`-row CPU protocol (where a few kilobytes of quantized real rows already cover a substantial fraction of the `340`-row training cap), `v3` trails raw quantized row subsampling by `mean ΔR = -0.0250 [-0.0297, -0.0201]` (`W/T_010/L = 1,919 / 7,481 / 3,428`). Upstream benchmark-family disjointness beyond exact `train_sha256` and untouched sealed confirmatory generalization remain open.
